basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disease defined by spinal/peripheral axonal degeneration and adrenal involvement; pigmentation and neurogenic sphincter symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Progressive neurodegeneration causes movement abnormalities and cognitive decline; acanthocytosis does not establish clinically significant blood damage.
Inherited epidermolytic palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; skin is the defining affected organ.
Neoplasm arising in or occupying the esophagus; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Myopathy 8/8 with neurologic abnormalities; sensorineural hearing loss 3/3. Cataract and hepatic failure have single-patient reports without established cohort prevalence.
ADCY5-related central movement disorder; hypotonia and weakness do not establish primary muscle injury. Cardiomyopathy and heart failure occur in 5-29%.
Defined by abnormal bone formation or resorption; a systemic metabolic disorder is not universal across the umbrella.
Squamous epithelial tumor of the ovary, a reproductive organ; no defining endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disease, heart defects and hypothyroidism define the syndrome; skeletal malformations occur in 30-79%. Ocular abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defining stapedial/external-ear malformations cause conductive deafness; persistent facial nerve palsy is a defining neurologic component.
Progeroid skin disease; keratoconjunctivitis sicca 2/3, dental eruption/crowding abnormalities 1-2/3, anemia/thrombocytopenia 1/3. Muscle atrophy 1/3 omitted by cap.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a malignant blood/marrow disease; the leukemia designation alone does not establish lymphoma or another commonly damaged organ.
Calculi occupy the kidneys or other urinary tract structures, all covered by the renal axis.
The spectrum includes intrinsic cytopenias/bone marrow failure and cerebellar ataxia. Myeloid neoplasm susceptibility does not itself add organ damage.
Inherited retinal phototransduction dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness.
Acquired factor XIII deficiency directly impairs coagulation; autoimmune inhibitors are one subgroup, not universal across acquired deficiency.
HLA-I expression immunodeficiency; destructive granulomatous skin ulcers affect roughly 30-50%. Respiratory infections and resulting bronchiectasis are secondary diseases.
Zinc-transport disorder with neurodegeneration and renal tubulopathy; persistent ptosis 4/4 and strabismus 3/3 support ocular dysfunction. Hypertension is secondary to nephropathy.
Intramuscular lipomatous tumor infiltrates skeletal muscle; adipocyte histology alone does not establish skin or subcutaneous involvement.
Scarring follicular keratosis affects skin and hair. Photophobia alone is insufficient; the supplied evidence does not establish damaging corneal disease in at least 30%.
Periodic paralysis is a skeletal muscle excitability disorder; potassium disturbances and endocrine causes vary across subtypes.
Defining radial-ray/diaphragmatic defects, cardiovascular malformations and omphalocele. Common pulmonary hypoplasia or other direct lung injury is not established.
Congenital duplication of digestive tract structures is a gastrointestinal malformation.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder affecting language and development; variable cardiac anomalies lack evidence of occurrence in at least 30%.
Infectious inflammation of the pelvic peritoneum is a form of peritonitis; involvement extends beyond the reproductive organs.
